confusing: Slide 2 'JAX-metal consider it dead' quote is a Jan 2026 maintainer comment framed as proof of a gap, not a benchmark

Slide 10 stacks 40x, 22x and 121x, three different ratios at once
doubts: 40x vs MuJoCo C rollout is planar 2D impulse contacts vs a 3D general solver, so not like-for-like physics

Walker diverges from MuJoCo after 0.6-0.8s; 'same answers' headline overstates it

questions: What does MuJoCo do at 4,096 envs per-thread on MJX CPU vs yours, with identical contact complexity?

confusing: Slide 13 'who it's for' has no number: zero users, zero revenue, no pricing
'Hosted classroom version and edu licenses' is one gray footnote, not a plan
Why now? Slide 2 gestures at NVIDIA-only but doesn't say why Mac RL demand is rising
Slide 12 admits agents wrote most of the code, so the moat is unclear
doubts: Planar 2D toy physics is a teaching tool; I doubt a real robotics team switches for it
RL classes are a tiny, price-sensitive market, and free Colab/MJX already serve them
Sim-to-sim transfer to MuJoCo says nothing about real robots, the only thing buyers pay for
87s install is on a warm cache for the author, not strangers
questions: Who pays, how much, and have a single class or club committed to using it?
